I1.title: Wi-Fi to the cloud
I1.heading: Publish readings to ThingSpeak
I1.goal: Join your Wi-Fi network, 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz, and post temperature and humidity from a DHT11 to a ThingSpeak channel every 20 seconds.
steps: Create a free ThingSpeak channel with two fields and copy its Write API Key.
Install DHT sensor library from the Library Manager.
Put your network name, password and key into the three constants at the top of the sketch.
Unplug USB, wire the DHT11, plug in and run the command.
The monitor prints the IP, channel and band, then HTTP 200 every 20 seconds. Watch the channel's charts fill.
I1.note: Unlike the C6, the C5 also joins 5 GHz networks: channel 36 and up. Never commit a sketch with your real password or key.

I2.title: Bluetooth LE touch
I2.heading: Notify a phone when you touch a pad
I2.goal: Turn the Pulsar C5 into a Bluetooth LE peripheral with one service and one characteristic that notifies touched or released from a TTP223B touch pad.
steps: Unplug USB, wire the touch pad, plug in and run the command.
On your phone, open nRF Connect or LightBlue and connect to PulsarC5-BLE.
Open the service and subscribe to the characteristic's notifications.
Touch the pad: the phone shows touched, then released.
I2.note: The C6 version notified four times a second whether or not anything changed; this one notifies only on a change, which keeps the radio quiet.
